fields.why: The 2018 vs 2022 state comparison (before/after) and state unit of analysis (ecologic) are agreed; the report is also a routine descriptive tracking of state policies (data feed the CDC STATE System), so adding surveillance/descriptive is defensible but not required.

The report measures progress in Medicaid (low-income) cessation coverage against the Healthy People 2030 target ('falls short of the Healthy People 2030 target of all 50 states and DC'), which meets the literal 'measures progress against a target' rule; A's false is defensible if the target must be a disparity target, since disparity framing appears only in background and implications.

brief_issues: equity_action: the brief should say whether 'progress against a target' requires a target defined in terms of a disparity or gap, or whether any target (e.g. a Healthy People policy target for a low-income population) qualifies.
